_comment: Story and lesson clue freeze. Holds every answer: never deploy (data/ is in .vercelignore). Regenerate ONLY after Joshua signs off on a clue, hint or wrong-answer reply: node scripts/ci/check-clues.mjs --update-stories

clues.hint: Returned is the instruction. Something in the line goes backwards, and only one word is short enough to turn round in four letters.
wrongReactions: "No." He does not look up. "Which word is doing the work? One of them tells you to turn something round."
"Returned. Something comes back the other way. Take the word just before it and read it backwards."
"M-A-I-L, returned. L-I-A-M. He has had the name a long time. Now take it up to the terminal."

clues.clue: Embracing towel comes with warm greeting (7)
clues.hint: The answer is not hiding behind the words. It is hiding INSIDE them. Read straight across "towel comes" and let the gap between the words disappear.
wrongReactions: "Not that one. Try reading the line letter by letter, straight through, and ignore where one word stops and the next starts."
"Closer. The word 'Embracing' is the instruction: something in this line is holding the answer inside it. Look hard at towel comes."
He traces the letters on the wet plank: "to-W-E-L-C-O-M-E-s. It was sitting there the whole time. Seven letters."

clues.clue: Face remodelled into a place for coffee (4)
clues.hint: The answer is an anagram. Look for a word whose letters can be rearranged.
wrongReactions: The fox shakes its head and scratches at the word "remodelled" on the stone.
The fox whines softly and nudges your hand. "Remodelled" means the letters are shuffled. Which four-letter word can be rearranged?
The fox huffs and paws at "face." Rearrange those four letters into a place that serves drinks.

clues.clue: Something instantly perky, starts a mouthful (3)
clues.hint: That's an initial letters clue. "Starts" tells you to take the first letter of each word before it.
wrongReactions: "Not quite. Take the first letter of each word: Something, Instantly, Perky. What do those spell?"
She traces the first letters on the counter with her finger: "S... I... P..."
"Three letters. S, I, P. What's a small mouthful of a drink?"

clues.hint: A hidden word clue: the answer is concealed within the words of the clue themselves, spanning across them.
wrongReactions: "Incorrect. Read the words again. The answer is spelled out across them, hidden in plain sight."
"Look where one word ends and the next begins. The letters bridge the gap."
"The answer sits across 'the road.' Four letters. Extract them."

clues.hint: A container clue: one word placed inside another. DE (Germany) embraces IN. The definition is "Eat."
wrongReactions: "DE is the abbreviation for Germany. IN is embraced by it. Place IN inside DE."
"D... IN... E. Put the letters together. What word means to eat?"
"D-I-N-E. IN, embraced by Germany. To dine is to eat."

clues.hint: A double definition clue: two separate definitions, both pointing to the same three-letter answer. A chart is one. A plan is the other.
wrongReactions: "Two definitions, one answer. What do you call a chart of the world?"
"Think about it: you chart a course. You also plan a route. What three-letter word means both?"
"M-A-P. A chart of the land, and to plan something out. Both meanings, one word."

clues.hint: Two words, two definitions, one answer. What word means "new" (as in a novel idea) AND is also a type of book?
wrongReactions: "Something original, something you read. Same word."
"N-O-V-E-L. A novel approach. A novel on the shelf."

clues.hint: Same idea: two separate definitions pointing to the same word. What word means "departs" (she leaves) AND also means "pages" (leaves of a book)?
wrongReactions: "She ___ the room. The ___ of the book. Same word."
"L-E-A-V-E-S. She leaves. The leaves of a manuscript."

clues.clue: Ache stirred after beginning of boating for a sandy shore (5)
clues.hint: 'Stirred' tells you the letters of 'ache' are jumbled. 'Beginning of boating' means take the first letter of 'boating'. The stirred letters come after it.
wrongReactions: "Not quite, but you're thinking. 'Beginning of boating' gives you the letter B. Mix that with A, C, H, E."
"You've got the letters B, E, A, C, H. What word meaning 'shore' can you make from those?"
He writes the five letters on the workbench with chalk: B, E, A, C, H. "Rearrange these. Where do you find sand and waves?"

clues.hint: 'Shattered' means rearrange. Rearrange R-A-G-E-S into a word meaning cogs.
wrongReactions: "Five letters: R, A, G, E, S. What turns inside a machine?"
"G-E-A-R-S. The cogs that make everything work."

clues.hint: 'Reworked' is an anagram indicator. Rearrange T-R-A-P-S into a word meaning components.
wrongReactions: "T, R, A, P, S. What do you call the components of a machine?"
"P-A-R-T-S. Traps reworked into parts."

clues.hint: "Broken" is the anagram indicator. Rearrange the letters of HORSE. The definition is "coastline."
wrongReactions: The crab clicks its claws impatiently. Rearrange the letters of "horse."
Five letters: H, O, R, S, E. What word meaning "coastline" can you spell?
S-H-O-R-E. The horse, broken apart, becomes the shore beneath your feet.

clues.hint: A deletion clue: "endlessly" tells you to remove the last letter. What word for "shelter" loses its final letter to become a bay?
wrongReactions: "What's a five-letter word for shelter? Now cut off the last letter."
"COVER is a shelter. Remove the last letter..."
"C-O-V-E-R without the R. A bay, right here around you."

clues.clue: Sculpt without right makes a hollow (4)
clues.hint: Another deletion clue: "without right" means remove the letter R. What word for "sculpt" loses an R to become a hollow?
wrongReactions: "What's a five-letter word for sculpt? Now remove the letter R."
"CARVE means to sculpt. Take away the R..."
"C-A-R-V-E without the R gives C-A-V-E. A hollow in the rock."

clues.clue: Tough about love, a dragon's pile (5)
clues.hint: A container clue. "Tough" gives you a word, and "about" tells you it wraps around something very small. In tennis, love means a score.
wrongReactions: "Think about what 'love' means on a tennis court, mate. It's not romance."
"HARD is tough. Now wrap it about the tennis score for love."
"HARD, holding the round score for love inside it. What do you call everything I sleep on?"

clues.clue: Iron fen forged into a blaze (7)
clues.hint: "Forged" is the anagram indicator. Melt the letters of IRON and FEN together. The definition is "a blaze."
wrongReactions: "Seven letters out of two words. 'Forged' is doing the work here."
"Iron and fen, into the forge together. What blaze comes out?"
"The letters of IRON FEN, melted and recast. A blaze big enough for a dragon."

clues.hint: "Strangely" is the anagram indicator, and it points at that odd word at the end. The definition is "Riches."
wrongReactions: "Austerer. Strange word, isn't it? Stranger still once you rearrange it."
"Eight letters in AUSTERER. Shuffle them into what fills this cavern."
"Funny thing about hoarding riches: it makes a dragon austerer. Now put those letters back in the right order."

clues.hint: This is a double definition. Both halves of the clue point to the same four-letter word. A blemish on a surface, and something you aim at.
wrongReactions: "Two definitions, one word. Think about what a blemish is. Think about what a target is."
"A stain or scratch on a surface. Something you aim for. Four letters."
"It's also a name. My name, in fact."

clues.hint: "Confused" is the anagram indicator. Rearrange the letters of TRACER. The definition is "lunar feature".
wrongReactions: "The word confused tells you to jumble up some letters. Which letters?"
"Take T-R-A-C-E-R and rearrange them. What lunar feature can you spell?"
"An anagram of TRACER gives you a six-letter word for a hole on the moon's surface."

clues.hint: Two mechanisms work together in this clue. "Shattered" is an anagram indicator: rearrange PIECES. "Left" gives a single letter (L) that slots inside the wreckage. The definition is "overshadow."
wrongReactions: "Two mechanisms, remember. Something shatters. Something small slips inside the wreckage."
"'Left' is one letter in crossword shorthand. Drop it into the shattered PIECES."
"Rearrange the letters of PIECES, then slide the L for 'left' inside them. The definition is 'overshadow'. Think of what the moon does to the sun, right where you're standing."

clues.hint: A double definition: two meanings, one word. Both "Celebrity" and "heavenly body" are separate definitions of the same four-letter word.
wrongReactions: "Two definitions. A famous person is one. A point of light in the sky is the other. Four letters."
"Think of someone on a red carpet. Now think of something twinkling above us. Same word."
She points upward. "S-T-A-R. A celebrity. A heavenly body. Both meanings, one word."

clues.hint: "In" is the hidden-word indicator: the answer is hiding inside the clue itself. The definition is "Stellar explosion." Read straight across the boundary of 'casino vault'.
wrongReactions: "The answer is hidden in plain sight. Let the words 'casino vault' run together and look between them."
"Take the end of 'casino' and the start of 'vault'. What burst of light do you see?"
She traces the letters with her finger: casi-NO VA-ult. "There it is, glowing between the words. A stellar explosion."

clues.hint: A charade: each part of the clue gives you a fragment to assemble. "Company" is a common abbreviation (2 letters). "Encountered" is a synonym (3 letters). Put them together. The definition is "celestial visitor."
wrongReactions: "Company has a standard short form. Two letters. You see it on business cards."
"CO is company. MET means encountered. Put them together. What visits us from deep space?"
She writes it piece by piece on the floor. "C-O from company. M-E-T from encountered. CO-MET. A celestial visitor with a tail of ice."

clues.clue: Head of household? Ring me, I live here! (4)
clues.hint: "Head of" means take the first letter. "Ring" is a round letter. Keep "me" just as it is.
wrongReactions: "Head of household" gives you the letter H. What shape is a ring?
H, then O (a ring), then ME. Put them together.
H-O-M-E. The head of Household, a ring (O), and ME.

clues.hint: A hidden word clue: the answer is tucked inside the surrounding words, spanning the gap between them. Look at where "savoy" ends and "agent" begins.
wrongReactions: "Not quite. Read the letters across the two words slowly: S-A-V-O-Y-A-G-E-N-T. See a journey hiding in there?"
"Start from the 'V' in 'savoy' and read six letters forward: V-O-Y-A-G-E."
"saVOYAGEnt. Six letters, right there in the middle. A journey."

clues.hint: 'Adrift' tells you to rearrange the letters of 'tacos.' The definition is "shoreline."
wrongReactions: "Five letters: T, A, C, O, S. What do you call the land where sea meets shore?"
"C-O-A-S-T. Tacos rearranged. I won that one at a beachside puzzle tournament."

clues.hint: A charade: build the answer out of pieces, front to back. "Mum" gives a two-letter word for mother. "Street" has a standard two-letter abbreviation. Bolt them together. The definition is "pole."
wrongReactions: "Think in fragments. What's the short word for mum? What's the abbreviation on every street sign?"
"MA is mum. ST is street. Bolt MA onto ST and you've got a ship's pole."

clues.hint: Think of a word that means both "to stagger" and "a spool used for fishing line."
wrongReactions: "Two definitions, one answer. What do you call it when someone staggers or sways?"
"Think about what holds the fishing line. A spool that you wind. It also means to stumble."
"R-E-E-L. You reel in a fish, and you reel from a shock. Four letters."

clues.clue: Vermin returning as a celestial body (4)
clues.hint: "Returning" tells you to reverse a word. "Vermin" = RATS. Reverse it.
wrongReactions: RATS is vermin. Read it backwards.
R-A-T-S backwards is S-T-A-R. A celestial body.

clues.hint: "Found in" is the indicator. Read across "maple aftermath": m-a-p-l-e-a-f-t-e-r-m-a-t-h. What page do you see spanning both words?
wrongReactions: Look at the letters where "maple" meets "aftermath": ...L-E-A-F...
map-L-E-A-F-termath. Four letters spanning the gap. A page.

clues.hint: "Drink" is the definition. "Initially" says take the first letters of "Taken Every Afternoon": T, E, A.
wrongReactions: "First letter of Taken = T. First of Every = E. First of Afternoon = A."
"T-E-A. A drink. The initials spell it out."

clues.hint: Rearrange S-T-E-A-L. What five-letter word meaning "stories" can you spell?
wrongReactions: "The letters are S, T, E, A, L. Jumble them into stories."
"T-A-L-E-S. Stories told around a campfire."

clues.hint: Put IN inside WE: W-IN-E. What drink is that?
wrongReactions: "W... then IN... then E. Put them together."
"W-I-N-E. We holding in. A drink."

clues.hint: What word means "not heavy" AND also means "illumination"?
wrongReactions: "Something that is not heavy. Something that provides illumination. Same word."
"L-I-G-H-T. A light load. A light in the darkness."

clues.clue: First of royal cue, broken, is a remedy (4)
clues.hint: "First of royal" = R. Now take R and CUE together and rearrange all four letters. What remedy do you get?
wrongReactions: First of "royal" gives you R. Add that to the letters C, U, E. Now scramble all four.
R, C, U, E scrambled. What word meaning "remedy" can you make?

clues.hint: Rearrange H-E-A-R-T into a five-letter word for the planet we live on.
wrongReactions: "Five letters from 'heart': H, E, A, R, T. Our planet."
"E-A-R-T-H. Heart shattered becomes Earth."

clues.hint: "Endlessly" means remove the last letter. SCARE without its final E...
wrongReactions: SCARE without its last letter. What are you left with?
S-C-A-R-E minus the E = S-C-A-R. A mark left behind.

clues.clue: Bargain event heard on a boat (4)
clues.hint: "Heard" = homophone indicator. A bargain event is a SALE. What sounds like SALE but belongs on a boat?
wrongReactions: "A bargain event is a SALE. What word sounds exactly like SALE but means something on a boat?"
"S-A-I-L. Same sound as SALE, different spelling. You sail on a boat."
